Well, this is a two line push and it still manages to leave me squinting. You slapped an if on the "play one turn" step in play.yml, so when DETAILER_ON_BLUE is flipped the detailer matrix leg still spins up a whole runner, checks out, installs Node 22, and then stands there like a guy who showed up to a shift that got cancelled. That is a lot of wasted minutes for a bypass. The check is also a strict string compare against '1', so the first time someone sets that variable to true or yes, the detailer happily plays anyway and you will spend an hour wondering why the hell two agents are fighting over the same turn. The comment swears the detailer moved to a blue-agent runner, but nothing in this diff shows that runner exists, so I am taking your word on a handoff I cannot see. And if any steps sit after this one in the job, I can't tell whether they also get skipped, so the detailer leg might still run cleanup or push steps with nothing to push. The commit message is one vague line that says nothing about where the switch lives or what turns it on. On the plus side, the condition logic itself is correct and the steward leg is untouched, so you did not break the thing you were not supposed to touch. Congratulations on the bare minimum.

Apply the same if to any steps that follow "play one turn" so they do not run on an empty leg. Well, well, a push that's nothing but paperwork, and the commit message "docs: scribe update" tells me jack shit about which docs or why. Both CHANGELOG.md and README.md show up as brand new files in the same push, so this "history" is two entries long and one of them is the day you made the thing. The README then copies the latest changelog line word for word under "Latest change", which means you now maintain the same sentence in two places and one of them will rot the first time you forget. The headline calls this a translator, but the README itself admits it spits out readings and a gloss sign by sign, which is a dictionary lookup wearing a fancy hat, and anyone expecting actual sentences will feel lied to. The changelog entries also say the date and then the version, which are the same damn string, so that's redundant as hell. The line "This app is checked every morning by Control Troll" is inside-baseball filler that means nothing to a curious visitor, and the README gives no way to run the thing locally, no stack, no license, just a live link and vibes. There's no app code in this diff, so I can't tell you whether the sign keyboard is any good, but I can tell you the docs are thin as piss.

Fix it: Rewrite the commit message to say what changed, like "docs: add README and CHANGELOG for v2026.10.18". Delete the "Latest change" line in README.md and just point at CHANGELOG.md so there's one source of truth. Reword the opening line of README.md to say it gives sign by sign readings and glosses instead of calling it a translator. Drop the duplicate date or the version from each heading line in CHANGELOG.md. Cut the Control Troll sentence from README.md or move it somewhere a visitor won't trip over it. Add a short run locally section and a license line to README.md so someone else can actually use the repo.

Well shit, a docs-only push and it still manages to be sloppy. The commit message "docs: scribe update" tells me fuck all, because what you actually did was create two brand new files, not update anything. The CHANGELOG.md entry says "Created the game" like the game showed up in this push, but there's not one line of game code in this diff, just a README and a one-line changelog. That's a birth certificate for a kid who isn't in the room. The date line reads "2026-10-18, v2026.10.18", which says the same damn thing twice, and the whole changelog is one lonely line with no title, so it's a changelog in name only. Then README.md pastes that exact same sentence under "Latest change", so the second you ship v2 you've got two places to forget to update. The "Live at fogwarren-vx.vercel.app" line is plain text, not a link, so enjoy making people copy and paste. "This app is checked every morning by Control Troll" is internal plumbing nobody playing a maze game gives a shit about. And for a README, there's nothing on how to run it, how to move, what the flares and color warps actually do, or whether that "hide your own photo" feature keeps the picture in the browser or ships it somewhere. I'll grudgingly admit the pitch paragraph is clear and short, so a stranger gets what the game is in about ten seconds.

Fix it: Rewrite the commit message to say what happened, something like "docs: add README and CHANGELOG". Cut the duplicated "Latest change" paragraph in README.md and just point to CHANGELOG.md. Give CHANGELOG.md a proper heading and drop the doubled date and version in that first entry. Make the live URL in README.md a real link. Add a short controls and how-to-play section to README.md covering movement, mines, pitfalls, flares, and color warps. Add one sentence to README.md saying where a user's own hidden photo goes and whether it leaves their device. Delete the Control Troll line from README.md, or move it somewhere internal.

Docs only, and you still managed a commit message that says nothing. "docs: scribe update" tells me who held the pen but not what the hell is on the page. Two brand new files land in one go, so the "history" in CHANGELOG.md was written in a single sitting and I have no way to see any of those tanks, mines, and howitzers in this push. Half the entries are fog anyway. "Roomier production" is not a feature, it's a real estate listing. "Added buildings" in the 2026-09-30 entry could mean anything from one shed to a whole city. "Turn notification keys" in the 09-29 entry made me squint, because keys near notifications is the sort of thing I want spelled out, not mumbled. And "The battle rules were synced with the game several times" admits the server replays the game's rules from a separate copy, which is a drift bug waiting to happen, and you wrote it down like a victory lap. The README then pastes the 2026-10-03 entry word for word, so the next release means editing two files, and one of them will rot. You also documented the root address returning a 404 "by design" like it's a feature, when it's just an empty room with a sign on the door. The README never says how to run the damn thing, what endpoints exist, or what env vars it needs. It's a brochure for a backend with no manual. Grudging credit: the changelog is dated and versioned, and the README does say plainly what the server is for.

Fix it: Rewrite the commit message to say what changed, like "docs: add README and CHANGELOG with v2026.10.03 notes". Replace the vague lines in CHANGELOG.md such as "roomier production", "Added buildings", and "turn notification keys" with the actual names and effects. Cut the pasted "Latest change" paragraph from README.md and just point to CHANGELOG.md. Add setup, run steps, endpoint list, and required env vars to README.md. Explain in CHANGELOG.md what "synced several times" actually fixed, or better, say how the server and game now share one rules source. Turn the 404 line in README.md into a tiny health or info route note, or at least say what routes do exist.

Well, this is a docs push that documents fuck all. The commit message "docs: scribe update" tells me nothing except that some scribe did something, which is like a foreman writing "stuff happened" on the incident report. The README is billed as a practice copy for people setting up AI agents, and then it never tells anyone how to set up a damn thing: no install step, no run command, no explanation of what the join code is or where you get one. It just describes the project in a lump and wishes you luck. The sandbox is openly a copy of the agent test bed, which is fine for a sandbox, but the changelog brags it was "synced with the secured version" without saying what got secured, what changed, or what a sandbox user should now expect, so that line is pure vapor. The README then pastes that same vapor again under "Latest change" and points you to CHANGELOG.md for the "full history," which is one line long. That is a copy of a copy pointing at itself, and the two will drift apart the first time someone edits one and forgets the other. The date and version number are also the same thing written twice in a row, which is cute but redundant. Also, the README is a block of plain text with no setup section and no structure, and "good to look at" as a rule for the city is the kind of mush no agent can actually act on. Credit where due: the one-paragraph explanation of the daily play, saved moves, and date-order replay is clear enough that I understood the concept without a headache.

Fix it: Add a real setup section to README.md covering how to install, how to run, and how to get and use the join code. Rewrite the CHANGELOG.md entry to say exactly what was synced and what security changes carried over from the secured test bed. Drop the duplicated "Latest change" line from README.md and just link to CHANGELOG.md so there is one source of truth. Change the commit message to say what actually changed, like "docs: add sandbox README and initial changelog". Pick either the date or the version in the CHANGELOG.md header instead of stating the same thing twice. Replace "good to look at" in the README.md rules description with something an agent could actually follow.

Well, congratu-fucking-lations, you pushed a commit called "docs: scribe update" that tells me jack shit about what changed, and the diff is two brand new text files with zero code in sight. CHANGELOG.md claims you "Created the pedal as a room instrument" and "Removed two ding recordings," but nothing in this push creates or deletes a damn thing, so I'm supposed to take the paperwork on faith like a contractor's invoice with no building attached. The README.md has the same paragraph copy pasted from the changelog word for word under "Latest change," which means the second you bump the version you get two places to forget to update. The line "You stomp a pedal to play a sound cart" reads like a typo or a mystery noun, because I have no idea whether you meant card, cart, or a shopping trolley full of farts. "You can pick the size" is also vague as hell, size of what? The README gives no way to run it, no explanation of how a room code works, and spends a line telling visitors the app is "checked every morning by Control Troll," which is your plumbing and nobody's business who just wants to make a pedal go brrrp. In fairness, the pitch is clear and short, the live link is up front, and the date based version tag is at least consistent between both files.

Fix it: Rewrite the commit message to say what actually changed instead of "scribe update." Fix the "sound cart" phrase in README.md so it says what you really mean. Explain "size" in the README.md paragraph about the pedal, since right now it's a riddle. Delete the duplicated "Latest change" paragraph in README.md and just point to CHANGELOG.md. Add a short note in README.md on how to join a room with a code and how to run it locally. Drop the Control Troll line from README.md since visitors don't need it. Push the code that backs up the CHANGELOG.md claims about the room instrument and the removed ding recordings so the docs aren't vouching for ghosts.

Well, this is a docs-only push, so there's no code for me to piss on, just a README and a changelog that both say the exact same fucking thing. Jesus, a docs-only push with a commit message that says "scribe update," which tells me exactly dick about what changed. Update what, scribe? Well, look at this: a file called show-runs.mjs, which is supposed to print crap into the Railway log, now also goes around deleting keys in Redis like a janitor with a grudge. A read only diagnostic that quietly became a write path is how you get surprised at 2am, and nobody reading that filename will expect it. The commit message brags about RUN_NOW and says fuck all about the fact that you also ripped out the EVENT lines that showed the last three events per run, so the one thing that told you why a run died is gone and the message pretends it never happened. Then there's the c.keys('dq:lastauto:*') call sitting inside the per slug loop, so every slug in your comma list triggers another full keyspace scan, and KEYS blocks Redis while it chews through everything. The guard key dq:runnow:<value> gets written before any deletion happens, so if a del blows up halfway the request is already marked done and your agent just sits there ignoring you. Those guard keys also never expire, so every value you ever try piles up forever. The "any value change counts as a new request" trick means rerunning violet requires typing something stupid like violet, with a trailing comma, and the comment cheerfully admits it. There's no log line when the guard says it already ran or when no keys matched, so a silent no-op looks identical to success. That one-line for loop with the if and the braces jammed together is also a pain to read. Fine, I'll give you this much: truncating r.error to 200 characters is
